content.title: About
content.content: Liquid coffee creamer is a ready‑to‑use product added to coffee to give it a smoother texture, creamy taste, and aromatic notes. It comes in a variety of flavors such as vanilla, caramel, hazelnut, and more.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Coffee creamer often contains vegetable oils like soy or coconut, plus emulsifiers that keep the mixture homogeneous.
Flavored versions may use natural extracts, but artificial flavorings are common for flavor stability.
Liquid creamer is convenient for office coffee machines because it dissolves instantly without frothing.
In some markets, creamer is sold in single‑serve sachets for one‑time use.

items.title: Mildens coffee bitterness
items.content: Cremers reduce the bitterness and acidity of coffee, making it more palatable for a wide audience.

items.title: Source of B‑vitamins
items.content: Certain formulations are fortified with riboflavin (B2) and cobalamin (B12), supporting energy metabolism.

items.title: Improves mouthfeel
items.content: Emulsifiers create a velvety, creamy consistency that enhances the drinking experience.

items.title: Soy or dairy allergy
items.content: Many creamers contain soy protein or dairy solids, which can trigger allergic reactions.

items.title: High sugar content
items.content: Flavored varieties often contain added sugars, which may be unsuitable for diabetics or those watching weight.

items.title: Trans fats
items.content: Some creamers use partially hydrogenated oils that contain trans fats, which are harmful to cardiovascular health.

content.title: How to Use
content.content: Add 10–30 ml of creamer to hot coffee, stir, and enjoy. It can also be used in iced coffees, lattes, cappuccinos, and dessert sauces.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store in the refrigerator after opening, tightly sealed, and use within 30 days. Do not freeze the product.
